line.name: Lampert 1675 Edición Verde
line.background_text: Edición Verde is the fifth blend released in Lampert's 1675 Edición Series, debuting at InterTabac 2025. Manufactured at AgroIndustrial Nicaraguense de Tabacos S.A.; each vitola is oval-pressed and uses tobacco aged five years, positioned as Lampert's fullest-bodied 1675 release to date. Only the Toro Grande ships to the U.S.; Robusto Grande and Short Robusto are Europe-only.

vitolas.summary_review: A medium-plus to full-bodied smoke dominated by gritty earth and creamy leather with dry hay, dark chocolate, oak, espresso, and cocoa nib notes; halfwheel scored it 86/100, finding the profile fairly straightforward.

critic_reviews.key_notes_text: 86/100; gritty earth, creamy leather, dry hay, dark chocolate, oak, espresso, cocoa nibs; medium-plus to full body.

vitolas.summary_review: European-market-only release; not distributed in the U.S. No independent review found.

research_notes: Confirmed distinct 1675 blend - Mexican San Andrés Negro wrapper, undisclosed binder/filler, five-year-aged tobacco, oval press, fuller strength target than Azúl/Rojo/Morado. NOTE: a separate, different product called 'Lampert 1593 Edición Verde' also exists (different numbered series) - do not conflate the two 'Verde' editions. 'Edición El Chapo' was also investigated as a possible 4th 1675 gap but could NOT be verified as a real product (see README) - excluded from this batch.
